- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or shows recent reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overshoots after a recent price spike (e.g., +5%+ above recent high) — apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 10–20% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — use sentiment smoothing (e.g., 3-day average) to dampen noise before forecasting.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model tends to err on the high side — adjust downward by 2–5% unless strong momentum is evident.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced when sentiment is volatile — apply a “sentiment-weighted decay” rule: reduce forecast magnitude by 10–15% if sentiment swings >0.5 in 3 days.
